title: Diamond in the Dirt
label: Polydor
format: CD and digital (per Wikipedia's Shystie discography table); album

type.basis: Album; reviewed in a 2004 grime round-up. One of the first major-label albums by a woman MC from the scene.

sound.text: A contemporary Vice review (2004) says she 'can rap' but finds much of the album so fast and high-pitched it is hard to follow; it singles out a game-show track and a live track with guitars as the standouts.

context.text: Lead single 'One Wish' entered the Official Singles Chart at no. 40 on 17/07/2004 (2 weeks) and reached no. 15 on the Official Hip Hop and R&B Singles Chart (OCC).
Wikipedia says 'One Wish' had no mainstream radio or music-TV support besides Channel U and MTV Base; it was later used in the 2006 film Kidulthood and on Dubplate Drama Vol. 1.

Shystie, from Hackney, first became known in 2003 for a white-label answer to Dizzee Rascal's 'I Luv U'; touring with Basement Jaxx, The Streets and 50 Cent led to her Polydor deal. The album sold about 60,000 UK copies and she was nominated for Best Newcomer at the 2004 MOBO Awards (Wikipedia).
Complex (2014) says she began on London pirate radio, getting her first break on Freek FM at about 17, and calls her 'the First Lady of grime'.

calls.label: grime (reviewed in a grime round-up column)

rels.other: Dizzee Rascal - I Luv U (her 2003 white-label response; not this album)
Kano (One Wish Remix, produced by Terror Danjah)

uncertainty: Catalogue number for the album not found; OCC catalogue 9866875 belongs to the 'One Wish' single. Vice's 2004 review prints the title as 'Diamond In the Dust'. Wikipedia lists AllMusic, BBC, Evening Standard, Guardian, Independent and Times Online reviews but the review texts were not opened. Producers uncredited in sources opened.
tracklist: 15 tracks per Wikipedia, opening with 'Intro' and 'One Wish'; includes 'Make It Easy', 'Questions (Game Show)', 'Bank Robbery' (feat. Ron, E Redeyez), and bonus tracks 'Armshouse' and 'Juiced'. Singles: 'One Wish' (5 July 2004; OCC catalogue 9866875, Polydor) and 'Make It Easy' (20 September 2004). Track-level producers not given by any source opened. The 'One Wish' B-side remix featured Kano and was produced by Terror Danjah (Wikipedia).
